therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: selective inhibition of RET mutations, fusions, and predicted resistant mutants
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: blocking oncogenic RET signaling in RET-altered solid tumors
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: participants with RET-altered solid tumors including NSCLC, thyroid cancer, and other advanced solid tumors
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Phase 1: MTD and RP2D; Phase 2: Overall Response Rate (ORR)

results.effect_size: ORR ranged from 56.7% to 85.2% across RET-altered tumor types
results.target_engagement_evidence: Dose-dependent changes in MAPK pathway biomarkers DUSP6 and SPRY4
biomarker_changes: DUSP6 decreased up to 81.57% at higher doses
SPRY4 showed variable changes with decreases up to 75.65% at higher doses
subgroup_findings: RET-fusion positive NSCLC with no prior systemic treatment: 78.3% ORR
RET-mutation MTC with no prior cabozantinib/vandetanib: 77.8% ORR
KIF5B fusion subgroup showed consistent high response rates across indications
safety_signals: Anemia was the most common serious adverse event
Febrile neutropenia occurred in 5/540 participants at 400 mg dose
Generally well tolerated with manageable toxicity profile

context.indication: RET-altered solid tumors including NSCLC, medullary thyroid cancer, papillary thyroid cancer, and other advanced solid tumors
